question:
**Direction: **In the question below are given three statements followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.

Statements:

All hens are pigeon.

No pigeon is crow.

All crows are peacock.

Conclusions:

No hen is a crow.

All hens are being peacock is possibility.
solution:
The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/abc14a9faf6d87bc7bdfaa887e741caee8f47ecf854ec7d0b6fda93bae51d9ae.png] 

Conclusion:

I. No hen is a crow → True

“All hens are pigeon.” and “No pigeon is crow”. Hence, “Definitely no hen is a crow”.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/abc14a9faf6d87bc7bdfaa887e741caee8f47ecf854ec7d0b6fda93bae51d9ae.png] 

II. All hens are being peacock is possibility → True

As we observed in the above Venn diagram, there is no relation between pigeon and peacock.

But there is a possibility

So we can conclude the given conclusion by the following possible Venn diagram. Hence, “All hens are being peacock is possibility” is true.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/13994d080bbc48def9f093301cd41ba1b7d860066fe230f7d13be048ac6fdd65.png] 

Hence, Both (I) and (II) follow is the correct answer.
